title: SDK Guardrails and Orchestration Quick Reference
author: Maya Thompson
summary: A compact, actionable reference for SDK maintainers and integrators covering onboarding guardrails, orchestration/fallback patterns, canonical fixes for top support symptoms, and docs-site operational steps for snippet and sample lifecycle.
body:
Purpose
This page is a single-page quick reference for developer experience engineers, SDK owners, and integration support to standardize safe defaults, automated fallbacks, and the minimal runbook required when customers hit common integration failure modes. It is intentionally concise and prescriptive — use the linked deep-dive playbooks for full procedures.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood client SDKs (javascript, python, go) and first-party adapter components (devx-sdk-proxy, sdk-sidecar).
- Covers onboarding defaults, runtime guardrails (timeouts, retries, circuit breakers), multi-model orchestration fallbacks, and the canonical recovery steps for support teams.
- Not a replacement for the SDK authoring guide or the full on-call runbooks; those are linked in Related Pages.

Owner and escalation
- Primary owner: Developer Experience (DevX) SDK team (owner contact: @maya.t@redwood.engineering).
- Pager escalation: eng-sre -> devx-oncall.
- Update cadence: review every quarter or when a major runtime change is merged (e.g., streaming API, auth changes).

Key SLOs and thresholds (recommended defaults)
- SDK call success: 99.9% 30d rolling for basic request/response paths.
- Client-visible latency: p95 < 200ms for non-streaming SDK calls (local dev loop).
- Streaming handoff/first-byte: p95 < 1s.
- Error budget triggers: >1% increase in 7d error rate -> open "devx-observability" ticket and run support playbook.

Onboarding guardrails (quick starters)
1) Local dev quickstart (recommended):
   - Install: npm install @redwood/inference-sdk or pip install redwood-sdk
   - Minimal config file (redwood.config.yaml):
     runtime: hosted
     api_key_env: REDWOOD_API_KEY
     region: us-west-2
     model: redwood/fastgen-v3

2) Safe defaults enforced in SDK:
   - Default timeout: 60s for generation endpoint, 10s for health calls.
   - Default max_tokens cap: 2048 (overrides to prevent runaway invoices).
   - Retry policy: 2 retries on 5xx, exponential backoff starting at 200ms, jitter 0-100ms.
   - Circuit breaker: open after 10 consecutive errors for 30s.

Runtime orchestration patterns
- Fallback stack (ordered):
  1) Preferred hosted model (fastgen-v3)
  2) Cost-optimized hosted quantized variant (fastgen-v3-q4)
  3) Regional fallback (eu-central-1 shard)
  4) Dedicated/reserved capacity endpoint (if customer has Dedicated)
  5) Degraded soft-response (structured placeholder + user-visible degrade message)

Implementation notes for SDK authors:
- Implement a pluggable RoutingPolicy interface. Default policy must be region-aware and tier-aware (hosted -> dedicated).
- Ensure KV/prefix cache keys are stable across model variant rollouts (avoid page-breaks on minor version changes).
- Telemetry emission for each decision: route.decide, fallback.triggered, cache.hit/miss (all as single-line JSON event).

Canonical fixes for top support issues (symptom -> immediate action -> root cause checks)
1) Symptom: High client-side timeouts and retries observed in logs.
   - Immediate action: Short-circuit client to a mock-local sandbox for customer (devx-sdk-proxy --mode sandbox).
   - Root cause checks: Check network MTU mismatches, SDK double-wrap retries (client+proxy), and long server-side queuing on runtime.
   - Fix: Apply client config override to disable client retries, engage SRE to inspect queue depth and backpressure metrics.

2) Symptom: Streaming responses truncated mid-transcript.
   - Immediate action: Ask customer to enable streaming debug in SDK (SDK env REDWOOD_STREAM_DEBUG=1), collect first-byte/last-byte timestamps.
   - Root cause checks: Inspect gateway keepalive, TLS termination idle timeouts, and SDK stream buffer sizes.
   - Fix: Increase connection keepalive on proxy to 90s, bump SDK stream buffer to 64KB, add SSE reconnect with resume token.

3) Symptom: Sudden spike in token usage from a single integration.
   - Immediate action: Set a tenant token cap (devx-admin set-cap --tenant <id> --tokens 10000/day) and contact customer success.
   - Root cause checks: Look for runaway loops, infinite generation prompts, or unbounded embeddings in background jobs.
   - Fix: Add client-side rate limiters and prompt length sanity checks (max_prompt_tokens 4096), add server-side alert on per-API-key burn rate.

Commands and snippets (copyable)
- Start local sandbox proxy:
  devx-sdk-proxy start --config redwood.config.yaml --mode sandbox --port 8023

- Minimal generation request (curl):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/fastgen-v3","prompt":"Summarize this dataset"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generation

- Fallback test harness (CI YAML snippet):
  steps:
    - name: run-fallback-smoke
      run: |
        python tests/fallback_smoke.py --primary redwood/fastgen-v3 --fallback redwood/fastgen-v3-q4

Docs-site operations (snippet lifecycle and release checklist)
- Snippet ownership: every snippet in the docs site must include a "snippet-owner" meta header that points to a team alias.
- Authoring flow for SDK examples: author -> local lint (snippet-ci) -> publish draft -> docs preview -> gated publish.
- Checklist to push a snippet change to production:
  1) Local preview renders (docs preview URL).
 2) Snippet lint passes (snippet-ci lint).
 3) Code sample executes in sandbox smoke test (CI).
  4) Update the example's metadata YAML with tested-sdk-version.
  5) Submit PR to docs repo with "docs: sdk snippet" tag.

Telemetry and query recipes (for rapid-TTR)
- Events to emit from SDK: sdk.request.start, sdk.request.end, sdk.fallback.called, sdk.retry.happened, sdk.circuit.opened.
- Minimal log line format (single-line JSON): {"ts": 1680000000, "event": "sdk.fallback.called", "tenant": "t-123", "route": "fastgen-v3-q4", "lat_ms": 120}
- Example splunk/metrics query to find fallbacks:
  index=sdk_events event=sdk.fallback.called | stats count by route, tenant | sort -count

Release and verification gates for SDK changes (mandatory)
- Unit tests with >= 95% coverage for routing logic.
- Integration tests: fallback smoke harness must run in CI and pass against the local sandbox.
- Docs: update snippet and include a runnable example with environment variables documented.
- Telemetry: emit a new metric for any behavior change and verify event schema compatibility.

Troubleshooting checklist (fast path)
1) Reproduce locally with sandbox proxy.
2) Collect single-run trace using env REDWOOD_TRACE=true.
3) If trace shows queuing: collect runtime queue depth and CPU/GPU utilization from perf dashboard (dashboards-and-alerts -> Runtime / Queue depth).
4) If trace shows network failures: collect tcpdump and compare SDK TLS settings with gateway TLS policy.
5) Escalate to eng-sre with collected artifacts.

Appendix: Suggested default config table
- default_timeout_generation: "60s"
- health_timeout: "10s"
- retry_policy: "retries=2, base=200ms, max=2s, jitter=0-100ms"
- circuit_breaker: "threshold=10, duration=30s"
- default_model: "redwood/fastgen-v3"

References
- Full SDK authoring guide: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-first-90-days-playbook-and-lab-recipes-2024
- Observability cookbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-observability-telemetry-cookbook-2026

Maintenance notes
- Who updates this page: DevX lead and the rotation oncall for SDK (update tag and commit history).
- When to retire: after 12 months of no changes or when the fallback stack or primary runtime changes significantly.
